issues.legal_issue: The expression “my heirs” in a will refers to legal heirs under the law of inheritance unless the will clearly indicates a different meaning.
material_facts: The will gave a son a life interest in specified property and provided that, if he died without male issue, “my heirs” would take the property.
The will did not specify a different class of heirs or indicate that “my heirs” meant only the testator’s issue.
issues.conclusion: The expression referred to the testator’s legal heirs under the law of intestate succession; it did not create an artificial class of residuary legatees.
issues.legal_principle: Legal terms such as “heirs” in a will are ordinarily construed in their legal sense unless a contrary intention is clearly expressed. “Heirs” is not normally limited to “issues.” The Court relied on Angurbala Mullick v. Debabrata Mullick, [1951] 2 SCR 1125, at p. 1144.

rule.if: will_construction_proceeding and will_names_heirs_as_recipients and not will_shows_different_meaning

predicates.will_construction_proceeding: The dispute concerns the construction of a will.
predicates.will_names_heirs_as_recipients: The testator provided that the testator’s heirs would take property upon a stated contingency.
predicates.will_shows_different_meaning: The will indicates that the term for heirs means a class other than the persons entitled under the law of inheritance.
predicates.named_heirs_are_legal_heirs: The persons described as heirs are those entitled under the law of inheritance.

issues.definition: When a will-construction proceeding concerns a will that names heirs as recipients and shows no different meaning, the named heirs are the legal heirs.

issues.legal_issue: Where a will makes devolution to the testator’s heirs depend on a life tenant dying without the specified issue, those heirs are ascertained under the succession law in force when that contingency occurs.
material_facts: The will provided that the testator’s son would have a life interest and that the testator’s heirs would take if the son died without male issue.
The testator died in 1928, and the son died without issue in 1957.
The will contemplated identifying the heirs when the son died without issue, when succession to the property opened.
issues.conclusion: The testator’s heirs had to be ascertained as if the testator had survived until the son’s death and died immediately afterward, under the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, then in force; applying that law did not give the Act retrospective effect.
issues.legal_principle: The will’s terms made the son’s death without male issue the event on which succession opened and required the testator’s heirs to be ascertained at that time. The Court applied the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as then in force, including sections 8 to 10, rather than the earlier Hindu law that had applied when the testator actually died. It treated this as giving effect to the will, not as applying the statute retrospectively.

rule.if: appeal_from_rejection_of_widow_claim and will_based_devolution_dispute and heirs_identified_when_contingency_occurs and contingency_occurs_after_succession_law_changes

predicates.appeal_from_rejection_of_widow_claim: A widow appeals after her claim to property under a will has been rejected.
predicates.will_based_devolution_dispute: The dispute concerns property devolving under a will’s directions.
predicates.heirs_identified_when_contingency_occurs: The will makes the identity of the recipients depend on a contingency and calls for their identification when it occurs.
predicates.contingency_occurs_after_succession_law_: The contingency occurs after the law governing succession has changed.
predicates.succession_law_at_contingency_governs_he: The heirs are identified under the succession law in force when the contingency occurs.

issues.definition: When a widow appeals a rejected claim in a will-based devolution dispute, the will calls for heirs to be identified when a contingency occurs, and the contingency follows a change in succession law, the law at the contingency governs heir identification.

issues.legal_issue: A widow who is a Class I heir of the testator as the widow of a predeceased son shares in the property under the statutory rules for distribution among heirs.
material_facts: On the assumption required by the will’s construction, the testator died intestate immediately after the son’s death without issue.
At that point the plaintiff was treated as the widow of a predeceased son, and the relevant family members fell in Class I of the statutory schedule.
The property was distributable among the plaintiff’s branch and the branches of the testator’s other two sons.
issues.conclusion: The widow was entitled to a one-third share, with the remaining two-thirds divided equally between the branches of the testator’s other two sons.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 8 and 9 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, Class I heirs inherit simultaneously to the exclusion of other heirs. Under section 10, Rules 3 and 4, heirs in the branch of a predeceased son take that branch’s share, and the widow and surviving children in that branch receive equal portions. Applying these provisions, the Court held that the widow was entitled to one-third of the property.

rule.if: appeal_from_rejection_of_widow_claim and intestate_heir_distribution_case and widow_is_class_one_heir and property_divided_among_three_branches

predicates.appeal_from_rejection_of_widow_claim: A widow appeals after her claim to property has been rejected.
predicates.intestate_heir_distribution_case: The dispute requires distribution of property among heirs as on intestacy.
predicates.widow_is_class_one_heir: The widow is a Class I heir as the widow of a predeceased son.
predicates.property_divided_among_three_branches: The property is distributed among the widow’s branch and two other family branches.
predicates.widow_entitled_to_branch_share: The widow is entitled to the share allocated to her branch.

issues.definition: In an intestate heir-distribution appeal, a widow who is a Class I heir and whose property is divided among her branch and two other branches is entitled to her branch’s share.
